assessment.text: The premise holds on this record: the board accepted Jen-Hsun Huang's resignation as President, CEO and director effective immediately, so 'Jensen is gone' is a fact, not a forecast.

The thesis needs a further step, that his departure makes the shares more attractive, and nothing in the record backs it; the filings can confirm the change but not why it happened or what it will do.

The operating record points the other way: the latest quarter under his leadership doubled revenue on a year earlier at the highest operating margin of the last eight quarters, so his tenure is not a problem whose removal would release value.

The corollaries that hold (revenue up, operating margin up, opex ratio down) all measure the quarter ended 2026-07-26, months before the 2026-11-12 filing, so they describe the business he left and say nothing about the effect of his exit.
What replaced him is an interim arrangement, with the CFO doubling as CEO while the board searches, which adds uncertainty rather than a defined new direction.

The valuation was set at the 2026-09-30 price, before the resignation, and needs 13.4% a year revenue growth for 10 years while leaning most on the 65.2% margin held every year; at the 90th-percentile industry margin it needs 28.1% a year, so a leadership change that dented margins would hurt the case rather than help it.

case_for.text: The departure did not come from a weakening business: revenue growth was speeding up, by 20.6 percentage points against the prior quarter, so the incoming leadership inherits momentum.
The margin gain came broadly from gross margin, R&D intensity and other operating costs rather than from one lever, which suggests the economics do not rest on a single decision-maker.
The interim CEO is the sitting CFO, so continuity in financial management is preserved through the search.

case_against.text: The record gives no mechanism by which losing the CEO under whom revenue grew 105.9% on a year earlier would raise value, so the 'because' rests on assumption alone.

The exit adds to a run of senior turnover in 2026, including the Chief Accounting Officer's retirement and the head of worldwide field operations' planned retirement, which deepens rather than resolves leadership risk.
Receivables grew faster than revenue, to 59.6 days against 54.1, a working-capital point a CFO also serving as interim CEO now has to manage alongside the search.

decides.text: Whether results after 2026-11-11 hold the growth and margin that the 2026-09-30 price already requires, which no filing in this record yet shows.
Who the board names as permanent CEO, and on what terms, since the interim arrangement leaves the direction undefined.
Whether any filing gives a reason his departure improves the outlook; without one the claim is a true fact attached to an unsupported conclusion.

would_change.text: An 8-K naming a permanent CEO would resolve the interim succession and give the thesis something to test.
A post-departure quarterly operating margin below the year-earlier 60.8% would show the change hurting the economics the price relies on.
Quarterly revenue after the departure falling below the $96.22B of the quarter ended 2026-07-26 would break the eight-quarter run of increases.

assessment.text: As worded the premise is false: fiscal 2026 revenue grew +65.5%, landing $45.06B short of the doubling line, and growth slowed by 48.7 percentage points from the year before.
The doubling the claim describes belongs to fiscal 2025, at +114.2%, so the claim most likely pinned the prior year's growth on the wrong fiscal year.
The shortfall is not a quirk of the revenue line: gross profit and operating income also failed to double in fiscal 2026, both missing by wider margins than revenue did.

The claim still points at something real, but on a different basis: in the newest quarter, Q2 FY2027, revenue grew 105.9% on a year earlier, so a doubling pace returned after the fiscal year closed, in one quarter rather than a full year.

For a buy decision the step from growth to price is what matters: at the 2026-09-30 price the reverse DCF needs 13.4% a year for 10 years, far below any recent year, but that leans most on a 65.2% operating margin holding every year, and at the industry's 90th-percentile margin of 26.6% the same price needs 28.1%.

The record cannot say whether the quarterly doubling lasts: among filers with revenue of at least $100.00B, 0 of 366 company-years showed a doubling, so the class offers no precedent for sustaining it at this size.

case_for.text: Even the slower fiscal 2026 growth of 65.5% ranked 6 of 63 in its industry, against a class median of 13.0%, and the newest quarter's 105.9% is back above the doubling line.
Deferred revenue rose +215.1% while revenue rose +105.9%, so billings ahead of delivery are growing faster than recognized sales, which is consistent with the recent pace not being exhausted.

case_against.text: Part of the growth is sitting in receivables: receivable days rose to 59.6 from 54.1, the balance grew +126.8% against revenue's +105.9%, and receivables also outpaced revenue across fiscal 2026 by +1.3 points.
Within SIC 3674, doubling held in 15 of 1045 company-years, and of the 12 that could be read a year later only 3 held again, so a doubling year has rarely repeated even among smaller chip makers.
The CEO resignation was filed 2026-11-12, after both the newest quarter and the 2026-09-30 price, so the record holds no revenue and no price that reflect it.

decides.text: The claim turns on basis: on the fiscal 2026 annual figure it fails clearly, while on the newest quarter's year-over-year figure a doubling is present.

For the decision, what matters is less whether fiscal 2026 doubled than whether growth and the 65.2% margin stay far enough above the 13.4% a year the price needs, with receivables collected rather than accumulating.

assessment.text: The premise is false on this record: in FY2026 free cash flow fell short of net income, so the claim fails as worded rather than on a technicality.
The shortfall is not a one-year blip: free cash flow as a share of net income has fallen at every reading, from 90.8% to 83.5% to 80.5%, and the prior year showed the same pattern.
Capex is not where the cash went; the gap opened before capex, in operating cash flow, where receivables rose $15.40B and inventory $11.32B.

The newest quarters widen the gap: over the four quarters to Q2 FY2027 conversion was 0.70x and Q2 alone was 0.40x, against 0.89x a year before, so the fiscal-year figure understates the current shortfall.

For the buy decision, the step that matters is that the price is set on earnings that are converting to cash less and less: the 28.5x earnings multiple sits beside a free cash flow yield of only 2.3%, both at the 2026-09-30 price.

Weak conversion is unusual for the company's size and industry: among SIC 3674 filers free cash flow above net income held in 582 of 911 company-years, and NVIDIA's cash conversion ranks 32 of 38 against a class median of 1.76x.

case_for.text: The claim points at something real even though it fails: free cash flow margin ranks 2 of 62 in the industry at 44.8%, so absolute cash generation is near the top of the class.
Because the shortfall sits in receivables and inventory rather than spending, it is the kind of gap that could narrow if those balances are collected or sold down, which a capex-driven gap would not.

case_against.text: Receivables grew faster than revenue in fiscal 2026, which is the opposite of what a cash-rich earnings stream implies and leaves more of reported income resting on collections still to come.
The trailing receivables build of $35.25B and inventory build of $16.61B are larger than the fiscal-year builds, so the working-capital drag is growing, not unwinding.

The reverse DCF leans on a 65.2% operating margin converting to cash at the assumed sales-to-capital ratio; a persistent working-capital drain makes that conversion assumption the weak link behind the 13.4% a year the price needs.

decides.text: The claim turns on whether the receivables and inventory build is timing that reverses or a lasting feature of how revenue is now earned; the record shows the build but not its cause, and later cash-flow statements and receivable balances would show which.

How often this lasts elsewhere is only a count: among filers with revenue of at least $100.00B, of 174 years where free cash flow beat net income, 125 still held a year later, which says nothing directly about whether NVIDIA's gap closes.

assessment.text: As worded, the claim cannot be tested on this record: no Data Center revenue line is computed, so the acceleration shown is for total company revenue, not the segment the thesis names.

For the whole company, the premise of acceleration holds, not just growth: year-on-year growth quickened in each of the last three quarters, from +73.2% to +85.2% to +105.9%, and the latest step was 20.6 percentage points.

Billing ahead of delivery is outrunning revenue, with deferred revenue up +215.1% against revenue up +105.9%, which points at demand still building rather than peaking; but receivable days also rose to 59.6 from 54.1, so part of the growth is not yet cash.

Against this, the company's own filing says it is effectively foreclosed from China's data center market, and that the threat of further export controls has already hurt demand, so the acceleration rests on a narrower customer base than before.

The step from acceleration to buying is weaker than the claim suggests: at the 2026-09-30 price, the reverse DCF needs only 13.4% a year for 10 years, so the price does not depend on acceleration continuing.

The reverse DCF leans most on the 65.2% operating margin holding; at the industry's 90th-percentile margin the same price needs 28.1% a year, so for the decision, margin durability matters more than the demand trajectory.

case_for.text: Revenue rose on the prior quarter in each of the last four quarters, and in each of the last 8, so the acceleration sits on an unbroken sequential run rather than an easy comparison.
Gross margin rose 2.6 percentage points on a year earlier to 75.0% while volumes surged, which suggests demand is outpacing supply rather than being bought with price cuts.

case_against.text: Inventory grew +111.0% while cost of revenue grew +86.8%, lifting inventory days to 119.3 from 105.6; product is building ahead of sales, which fits supply racing ahead of demand as well as it fits strong demand.
Total revenue includes gaming and workstation products still shipped to China, so it can accelerate even while data center demand faces a lost market and export-control drag.
Receivables grew +126.8%, faster than revenue's +105.9%, so a growing share of the reported acceleration is booked but not yet collected.

decides.text: The claim turns on the Data Center segment line in the filings, which this record does not compute; that line, not total revenue, would show whether the named demand is accelerating.
Whether the China foreclosure and the export-control risk show up as slower growth in the quarters after Q2 FY2027 is beyond what this record can show.
The CEO's resignation, filed 2026-11-12, came after the latest quarter; this record cannot say whether it affects customer demand.

analytics.label: Revenue growth the price implies (reverse DCF)
analytics.question: What growth does the price already assume?
analytics.formula: PV(g) = enterprise value $5.48T, solved for g between −50% and +100%
analytics.reading: At these assumptions the enterprise value of $5.48T needs revenue to grow 13.4% a year for 10 years, from $302.97B to $1.07T. The company's own revenue grew +100.0% a year over its last three fiscal years. The largest revenue any filer reported for 2025 is $716.92B (AMAZON.COM, INC.): the implied year-10 revenue is 1.5 times that. Of 40 ten-year spans of filers that started at its size (revenue of $151.48B to $605.94B; starts 2009 to 2015), 0 grew at least that fast (median 1.3% a year, 90th percentile 8.0%; 4 more could not be followed for ten years). With the operating margin at the industry's median of 4.2% (n = 61, 2025) instead of 65.2%, no growth from −50% to +100% a year reaches the price. With the operating margin at the industry's 90th percentile of 26.6% (n = 61, 2025) instead of 65.2%, the same price needs 28.1% a year. Across the grid (discount rate ±2 points, margin ±5 points) the implied growth runs from 6.5% to 19.7% a year (15 of 15 cells solve).
analytics.note: Arithmetic under stated assumptions, not a forecast and not advice: it says what constant growth the price would need if every assumption below held. Starting revenue $302.97B (Revenue, four quarters ended 2026-07-26). Operating margin 65.2%, every year: the trailing operating margin, $197.58B ÷ $302.97B. Tax on operating profit 21% (the US federal rate, a stated default). Sales-to-capital 1.47: trailing revenue $302.97B ÷ invested capital $205.76B (equity $228.98B + debt $33.37B − cash and securities $56.59B, 2026-07-26); each dollar of new revenue is assumed to need capital at this ratio. Discount rate 9% a year (a stated default, near a long-run US equity return). After 10 years, growth of 3% a year forever. Cash flow = revenue × margin × (1 − tax) − (revenue − last year's revenue) ÷ sales-to-capital; discounted at the end of each year; compared with the enterprise value. An implied growth is arithmetic: the growth at which a discounted cash flow under the stated assumptions equals the price. Change an assumption and it changes; it is not a forecast and not a price target. analysis.corollary_rule: A corollary is an implication a model proposed and code computed. Each is read by the grammar and by the typed form the proposing model wrote: two readers, which is weaker than the two-of-three rule the thesis's own claims are read under. A corollary never moves a verdict; when most of a claim's computed corollaries come out against it, the claim is flagged.
analysis.audit_rule: A sentence is verified by code when every id it cites is in this run, at least one is evidence, and every number it writes is carried by that evidence: a verified finding's quotes and cited figures, an analytic's value, inputs and reading, a computed test's operands and result, a reported figure, an 8-K event's text. The claim's own words carry no number, and neither does the sentence a model wrote for a corollary: only what code computed for it does. A threshold is a third thing: when a number equals the threshold of a computed test or corollary the sentence cites, or a condition's own threshold, the sentence is not failed for it, and it is listed as a threshold restated, not checked as a fact. A bare year is carried by a cited item dated in that year. The audit does not decide whether a sentence follows from what it cites.
analysis.persistence_method: Resampling with replacement: 10,000 paths of 4 quarters, each step drawn from the measure's own last N quarterly changes (differences in points for a percent, growth rates for an amount), from the current value; the share of paths in which the test holds in every one of the 4 quarters. Seed 20261118. It assumes the past changes are exchangeable: it ignores trend, seasonality and anything not in the facts. It describes the history; it is not a forecast.

weakest_why.text: The premise is true, but the step from the departure to buying has nothing behind it. Every corollary that holds measures the quarter ended 2026-07-26, so they describe the business he left, not the effect of his leaving.

The replacement is an interim CFO doubling as CEO while the board searches. It follows earlier 2026 departures of the chief accounting officer and the head of worldwide field operations, so the record shows rising leadership uncertainty rather than a defined improvement.

A leadership change could only help this valuation if margins hold. At the industry's 90th-percentile margin of 26.6%, the same price needs 28.1% a year, so any margin damage from the transition cuts against the thesis.

strongest_for.text: Demand looks to be building rather than peaking at the total-company level. Year-on-year growth quickened in each of the last three quarters, and deferred revenue grew +215.1% against revenue growth of +105.9%.

The margin base is unusually strong. Gross margin ranks 4 of 63 in its industry, and the 70% test has room of 1.69x a typical move. In 69% of resampled paths of its past changes, the test held for four more quarters; that describes history, not a forecast.

On the 2026-09-30 price, the implied 13.4% a year sits far below the company's own +100.0% a year over three fiscal years. Across the grid of assumptions, the implied growth stays between 6.5% and 19.7%.

strongest_against.text: The implied path has no precedent at this size. None of 40 ten-year spans of filers starting at its size grew that fast, the 90th percentile was 8.0%, and the implied year-10 revenue is 1.5 times the largest filer's revenue.
Growth is increasingly tied up in working capital. Receivables grew +126.8% against revenue growth of +105.9%, inventory days rose to 119.3 from 105.6, and Q2 conversion was only 0.40x.
The company itself says it is effectively foreclosed from China's data center market and that export-control risk has already hurt demand. That risk now meets an interim leadership arrangement.

bottom_line.text: The thesis's stated reason is unsupported. The record confirms that Huang has gone, but nothing in it shows his departure makes the shares more attractive, and the last quarter under him had the highest operating margin of the eight quarters shown.

The factual props split. Gross margin above 70% holds, and total revenue growth is accelerating. But fiscal 2026 revenue did not double, and free cash flow fell short of net income, so the thesis's numbers are half right on their own terms.

bottom_line.text: The only valuation in the record uses the 2026-09-30 price, which predates the 2026-11-12 resignation filing, so it cannot show how the market has priced the departure. It needs 13.4% a year for 10 years and leans most on a 65.2% operating margin holding every year.
The sharpest tension is between earnings and cash. The price is 28.5x earnings but only a 2.3% free cash flow yield, because net income is converting to operating cash at 0.70x over four quarters.

The record cannot say why Huang left, who will succeed him, or what results look like after the quarter ended 2026-07-26. A careful investor would want the 8-K naming a permanent CEO, the first 10-Q covering the period after the departure, and a Data Center segment line, which this record does not compute.
